finding.title: Remove the unused HierarchyLevelProgress.levelLabel field and its 'Level 1'/'Level 2' fallback computation
finding.why: hierarchy_progress_card.dart (the only production consumer of HierarchyLevelProgress) reads level.level and level.levelName, never level.levelLabel — a whole-tree grep for '.levelLabel' turns up zero non-definitional reads outside this field's own computation and test call sites. The field, its threading through CurriculumProgressService's three private builder methods, and its hardcoded 'Level 1'/'Level 2' English fallback are all computed on every progress-screen load for no consumer; that fallback would itself have been an AX-2 violation had this field ever actually reached a Text widget.
finding.recommendation: Delete HierarchyLevelProgress.levelLabel, the levelLabel/levelLabels parameters through CurriculumProgressService's builder methods, and update the ~15 test call sites that currently pass/assert it.
acceptance_criteria: grep -rn '\.levelLabel\b' lib/ test/ (excluding the removed definition) returns no hits after the change; curriculum_progress_service_test.dart assertions are updated accordingly.

finding.title: Fix Makefile check-15 cross-feature-import grep — it can structurally never detect a violation
finding.rule: Rule 2 (cross-feature deep imports) / Rule 0 checker correctness / AG-11

evidence.quote: awk -F: '{match($$1, /features\/([^\/]+)\//, a); match($$0, /features\/([^\/]+)\//, b); if(a[1] != b[1]) print}'

finding.why: match($0, /features\/([^\/]+)\//, b) re-scans the WHOLE line (path:linenum:import-text) for the leftmost 'features/X/' substring, which is always inside the file-path field that a[1] already captured — so b[1] is always identical to a[1] and the check can never print a WARN, no matter how many real cross-feature deep imports exist. I reproduced the exact pipeline against a real offending line and confirmed a[1]=b[1]='progress' even though the import target feature is 'content_browsing'. As a direct, concrete consequence, siyumim_grouped_view.dart:10 deep-imports content_browsing's provider file instead of the (currently empty) content_browsing.dart barrel, and make audit reports check 15 as clean regardless. The correctly-written custom_lint equivalent (no_feature_cross_import, ERROR severity) would catch this, but that tool currently crashes on every run — so both enforcement layers for Rule 2 are simultaneously non-functional, for two unrelated reasons, and nobody would know new violations are accumulating.
finding.recommendation: Rewrite the awk to isolate the imported feature name from the import-URI field only (not re-scan $0), add a Makefile-test fixture proving check 15 fires on a synthetic cross-feature deep import and stays silent on a same-feature one, then re-run make audit to see and triage the real (likely multi-file) backlog this uncovers across lib/features/.
acceptance_criteria: A fixture cross-feature deep import makes check 15 print a WARN; a same-feature deep import does not.
make audit re-run after the fix lists siyumim_grouped_view.dart:10 under check 15.
Decision recorded on whether the newly-surfaced backlog gets baselined (like the 32 Rule-1 edges) or fixed before check 15 can be promoted off warn-only.

finding.title: Centralize the 29 raw Color(0x...) hex literals in progress widgets into core/theme tokens
finding.rule: no_color_literal_outside_theme (custom_lint rule, currently non-functional because the tool crashes)
finding.why: The custom_lint rule that bans this exists and is correctly written but the tool crashes on every invocation, so nothing currently enforces it (29 call sites across 8 of the batch's 15 widget files, 15 of them in lifetime_folder_styled_widgets.dart alone). The cost isn't hypothetical: the identical 'active-day' blue (0xFF103BAC) is independently retyped in both streak_calendar.dart:219 and monthly_activity_sliver_calendar.dart:347, and the identical amber (0xFFFFD26A) is independently retyped in lifetime_folder_styled_widgets.dart:379 and :517 — proof that without a shared token, a future brand-color tweak requires hunting every file by eye and will eventually miss one, producing a visibly inconsistent color for the same semantic state.
finding.recommendation: Add named constants to core/theme/app_colors.dart (or app_theme.dart) for each distinct value and replace the 29 call sites; once custom_lint is unbroken (tracked separately), no_color_literal_outside_theme prevents regression.
acceptance_criteria: no_color_literal_outside_theme passes clean on this directory once custom_lint is functional again.

finding.title: Delete or wire up the dead MonthlyActivitySliverCalendar spike widget
finding.rule: Dead code / AG-4 duplicate top-level name

evidence.quote: /// This widget is **not wired into any screen yet** — it is a layout proof of

finding.why: The device-freeze problem this widget was built to solve (~9,600 daily cells for an All Time streak calendar) was actually solved a different way: recent_activity_screen.dart swaps in a totals-only _AllTimeSummaryCard for the All Time range instead of ever rendering a per-day grid. So this 404-line widget — plus its own hand-rolled MonthlyActivityRollup class, which duplicates the name of the real Drift-generated MonthlyActivityRollup in core/database/tables/monthly_activity_rollups.dart (its own doc comment at lines 4-12 flags this as a temporary stand-in to delete once wired in) — has no live caller and is exercised only by its own dedicated spike test. It sits in lib/ counting toward file-size/symbol-count backlogs for a problem the team already solved elsewhere.
finding.recommendation: Delete monthly_activity_sliver_calendar.dart and its spike test, or file a follow-up to actually wire it in and delete the hand-rolled MonthlyActivityRollup DTO in favor of the generated one. Don't leave a superseded proof-of-concept in the production lib/ tree.
acceptance_criteria: grep -rn MonthlyActivitySliverCalendar lib/ finds either zero results (deleted) or a real screen-level caller (wired in).

finding.title: Localize MonthlyActivitySliverCalendar's hardcoded English strings
finding.rule: AX-2 (no hardcoded user-facing strings; AppLocalizations/ARB with ICU plurals)

evidence.quote: return const Center(child: Text('No activity data'));

finding.why: Every other widget in this EN/HE batch routes text through AppLocalizations, but this file hand-rolls English-only pluralization with a raw ternary. It's currently unreachable (see the companion dead-code finding) so no Hebrew user sees it today — but if anyone wires this widget into a screen without noticing, it ships untranslated text into the Hebrew build silently, since no grep in this repo's audit checks widget files for bare Text('literal') calls.
finding.recommendation: If the widget is kept, replace the three literals with AppLocalizations getters and ICU plural messages before it is ever attached to a route.
acceptance_criteria: No bare string literal is passed to Text(...) in this file; make arb-parity stays green after adding the new keys.
